# Timeline of Modern Fraud Detection Approaches for Highly Imbalanced Transaction Datasets

**Question:** Compare modern approaches for detecting fraud in highly imbalanced transaction datasets, including how such models should be evaluated.

## Summary

The proposed FID-SOM method has demonstrated its ability to perform on par with, if not surpass, existing methodologies. [S4] The Numbers Game: In datasets spanning 2019–2020, months with only 258 fraudulent transactions among 139,538 total transactions (0.18%) were observed. The European Bank Authority’s 2024 report shows fraud represents only 0.015% of total card payments in Q1 2023. [S5] Electronic companies anticipate a surge in fraudulent transactions globally, resulting in losses of 40.62 billion USD by 2027, with fraudulent transactions increasing from 9.84 billion USD in 2011 to 32.39 billion USD in 2020. [S1]

## Limitations

- The evidence does not specify the exact impact of data preprocessing techniques on model performance beyond the application of SMOTE.
- The evidence does not provide detailed information on the failure modes of fraud detection models in real-world transaction environments beyond concept drift and high-dimensional categorical features.
- The evidence does not clarify the conditions under which traditional evaluation metrics fail for fraud detection models beyond the thought experiment example.
